title: Strength for the Battle
scripture: But they that wait upon the Lord shall renew their strength...
reflection: Not every season of divine compensation begins with an outward change. Sometimes the first gift is strength to keep standing when circumstances remain demanding. Weariness can make ordinary responsibilities feel impossible, and prolonged pressure can weaken hope. Isaiah reminds God’s people that human strength has limits, but the Lord does not grow weary. Waiting upon Him is not passive resignation; it is a posture of trust that seeks His help, receives His Word, and continues in obedience with renewed dependence.

A runner who has trained well still needs to manage energy over a long race. Trying to sprint every mile may lead to exhaustion before the finish. Likewise, do not confuse faithfulness with refusing rest or pretending you never struggle. Pray honestly, seek wise support, care for your body, and break overwhelming tasks into manageable steps. God can renew you through Scripture, worship, fellowship and practical help. Ask not only for the situation to change, but also for the strength and wisdom to walk through it well. Renewed strength is itself a precious expression of God’s sustaining grace.
prayer: Lord, renew my strength where I have grown weary. Help me wait on You, receive Your help, and continue with courage and wisdom. In Jesus’ Name. Amen.
author: Rev. Iniobong Udoh
